sentences.text: Shri Dayaram Vishwakarma - Public Prosecutor for respon Heard on admission.
Appeal, being arguable, is admitted for hearing.
Heard on I.A. No.2441 of 2025, second application under Section 430 of BNSS for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
His first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail has been dismissed vide order dated 14.06.2023.

2. This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 26.10.2021 passed by Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act), Panna in Special Case No.34 of 2018 whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) (N) and 342 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for three years, R.I. for five years, R.I. for 10 years and R.R. for three months, respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act), Panna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the present appellant has suffered the total jail sentence of 8 years and 3 months.
The maximum punishment awarded to him is 10 years rigorous imprisonment out of which more than 80% of sentence has been served out by him.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix sustained no injury on her person.
She remained with the present appellant for seven days, hence, it is a case of consent.
It is further submitted that the jail sentence of other two co-accused persons have been 2 CRA-8243-2022 suspended and they have already been released on bail by this Court.
The FSL report is also negative.
It is further pointed out that there are various contradictions and omissions in the statements of the prosecution witnesses.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
It is also submitted that the present appellant is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by the Court.

Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant is entitled to be given the benefit of suspension of sentence.
4.
Per contra , learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the various contradictions and omissions revealed from the statements of the prosecution witnesses, but without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No.2441 of 2025 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.70,000/-
(Rupees Seventy thousand Only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 07.10.2025 and on subsequent dates given by the trial Court in this regard,
till final disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
